sentences.text: Triunfosaurus was a medium-sized sauropod dinosaur.
Vertebrae located near the front of the tail possess short, robust prezygapophyses that are slightly angled upwards from the horizontal plane.
The rear sides of the vertebral centra are strongly concave, while the pleurocoels, which are depressions on the sides, are relatively small.
The internal texture of the vertebrae is not sponge-like or camellate.
Neural spines on the vertebrae are small and feature midline processes that expand near the top.
Two small crests at the base of the posterior hemal arch form a crest-like structure.
The ischium has a unique shape where the pubic contact area is half the total height and the shaft angles less than 70 degrees relative to the femoral articulation.
This specific bone proportion sets the animal apart from every other known titanosaur.
More than 535 individual dinosaur trackways have been discovered in the nearby Triunfo Basin.
Some of these footprints were likely made by Triunfosaurus itself.
The holotype fossil was discovered in sandstone layers of the Rio Piranhas Formation in the state of Paraíba, Brazil.
This specimen is a partial skeleton containing three tail vertebrae, three chevrons, three neural spines, and a right ischium.
The species Triunfosaurus leonardii was named and described in 2017 by a team of six researchers led by Ismar de Souza Carvalho.
The genus name combines the Triunfo Basin with the Greek suffix for lizard, while the species name honors paleontologist Giuseppe Leonardi.
The environment where the animal lived likely consisted of alluvial fans and river systems.
Triunfosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
The parent group of this dinosaur is Somphospondyli.
The animal was initially classified as a basal titanosaur but was later reassigned to the Somphospondyli due to conflicting evidence.
A 2026 redescription by Mannion and Carvalho interprets Triunfosaurus leonardii as a member of Somphospondyli belonging to or closely related to Titanosauria.
The Rio Piranhas Formation, where fossils were found, is dated to the Berriasian to Valanginian stages, possibly extending into the Hauterivian.
Triunfosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 145 to 130 million years ago, in what is now South America.
The holotype was found in the Rio Piranhas Formation in Brazil, dating from the Berriasian to Hauterivian, approximately 145 to 130 million years ago.
Triunfosaurus lived during the Berriasian to Hauterivian, from 143.1 to 125.77 million years ago.
Researchers argue that the feature used to classify Triunfosaurus as a titanosaur is also found in non-titanosaur somphospondylans like Phuwiangosaurus and Tangvayosaurus.
The assignment of certain tail vertebrae to the middle of the tail is questioned by some researchers.
Due to the problematic nature of the fossil evidence, some researchers have reassigned Triunfosaurus to the Somphospondyli rather than Titanosauria.
While Triunfosaurus was initially used to support a Gondwanan origin for titanosaurs, an alternate hypothesis suggesting dispersal from Europe remains plausible.
Poropat et al. reassigned Triunfosaurus to Somphospondyli, unable to confidently support its affinities with titanosaurs due to its problematic nature.
An alternative hypothesis involving dispersal from Europe remains plausible.
